subject: NimbusL2: compatibility hold + proposed launch window impact
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NimbusL2 nightly -> quantized variant failing kernel selection (inc log)

Hi Kim, Karthik —

Quick heads-up from the intake pipeline: the NimbusL2 (2.1) quantized "nimbusl2-int8" variant is failing our nightly compatibility runs on both A100 and H100 stacks. The failure is deterministic: kernel mismatch during compilation (see snippet attached). I ran the model through the staging runner and saw degraded perf and a fallback to a slower dispatch path; this causes latency SLOs to be missed in the 512/1024 token tails.

Summary: 
- Test: nightly-compat-20260810
- Error: kernel_select_fail -> fallback path 0x7f1a (attached log)
- Impact: estimated 15-25% tail-latency regression on heavy prompt workloads

I attached a short compat report (nimbusl2-compat-report.pdf) and the failing logs. Notably, the float16 variant appears fine.

Asking: do we want to hold the NimbusL2 quantized variant from being added to the public catalog / pinned rollout until infra/compilation have a patch? If so, request a temporary pin to the float16 variant for the launch window.

Next steps I recommend:
- decision on temporary pin + scope (catalog vs default runtime)
- an infra ticket to reproduce and patch kernel selection (I can triage)
- a canary plan if we unblock with a patch (I sketched one in the playbook)

Thanks —
Dev

--
Dev Patel
Senior Inference Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sophia Reyes <sophia.reyes@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimbusL2 nightly -> quantized variant failing kernel selection (inc log)

Thanks for the fast triage, Dev. Good catch.

Karthik — tagging you because this impacts our launch cadence for NimbusL2 with Acme.ai (they're expecting the quantized flavor in the "general availability" window we promised). Can we get an infra assessment on risk/time to fix?

I'm inclined to:
- request a temporary pin of the default "catalog" mapping to the float16 variant for the initial GA rollout (no public promotion of nimbusl2-int8)
- allow private dedicated customers (e.g., Acme) to opt into the int8 if they accept a lower SLO and sign an exception

Laura — can you coordinate a short note to Acme explaining the temporary hold and asking whether they want opt-in access (we should be explicit about perf tradeoffs)? I'll draft language but need your sign-off for the customer comms.

Also attaching a canary playbook sketch (nimbusl2-canary-playbook.md) Dev mentioned — it has the rollback criteria, telemetry events to monitor, and a canary cohort size recommendation.

If we pin, please include the scope: 1) catalog default -> float16; 2) runtime default mapping for hosted API; 3) note in release notes about int8 being experimental.

Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Product Manager, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimbusL2 nightly -> quantized variant failing kernel selection (inc log)

Appreciate the detail, Dev. Initial read: this looks like the kernel matcher is choosing a custom tiled GEMM path that isn't implemented for the new attention layout in nimbusl2-int8. I can't give a final ETA without a reproducer, but we have two parallel options:

1) Fast path (2-3 days): implement a runtime fallback that forces the compatible GEMM path for nimbusl2-int8 on the affected sequence lengths (explicitly keeps the older kernel). This is low-risk but may cost ~5% perf on A100.

2) Medium path (1-2 weeks): implement the new kernel and update kernel-selection guards; requires QA and an engineering rollout.

Recommendation: do a temporary pin for the public catalog -> float16 (Kim, +1 from me) and offer an opt-in exception for key partners. We'll T-shirt ETA for patch depending on which path we take.

Action items I'll take ownership of:
- create infra ticket with reproducer and assign to runtime team
- draft a safe default patch for the fast path with telemetry hooks
- coordinate canary rollout (use playbook attached)

If Acme wants private access, we should provide a waiver that outlines the SLO delta and a recommended canary cohort.

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Sophia Reyes <sophia.reyes@acme.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: partners@cloudmarket.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimbusL2 nightly -> quantized variant failing kernel selection (inc log)

Hi Kim —

Thanks for the update and for flagging this internally. Acme's timeline is: we planned to enable nimbusl2-int8 in our sandbox by Aug 20 and flip to prod mid-September pending performance verification. If you pin the catalog to float16 for GA, we'll need either (A) an opt-in private test instance to evaluate int8 despite the risk, or (B) a firm ETA for when int8 is safe to enable.

We prefer option A for the short term so we can validate real prompts. Can you confirm what the opt-in steps are, and any paperwork (exception form) we need to sign? Also please confirm whether the opt-in will expose Acme to event-level telemetry (we require that telemetry is shared via our integration).

Appreciate the transparent comms.

—Sophia

Sophia Reyes
Senior ML Engineer, Model Integrations
Acme.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophia Reyes <sophia.reyes@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimbusL2 nightly -> quantized variant failing kernel selection (inc log)

Thanks all — quick status update and decisions: 

1) Decision: we will pin the public catalog default for NimbusL2 to the float16 variant for the upcoming GA window. We will not promote nimbusl2-int8 to the public catalog until the kernel-selection patch is validated.

2) Opt-in for partners: Acme (Sophia) — we can provide a private opt-in build. Laura, please send the exception agreement and checklist (SLO delta, telemetry opt-in, and the canary cohort instructions). Dev/Karthik will attach the canary playbook and the known perf caveats.

3) Timeline: Karthik will open the infra ticket today. Fast-path patch target (if chosen) is 2-3 business days; medium path is 1-2 weeks. We'll prioritize the fast path to restore int8 perf sooner.

4) Communication: Laura, please draft the customer note saying "temporary catalog pin to float16 for GA; private opt-in available; int8 will be labeled experimental until validated." I will review and send to Sophia.

5) Follow-up: we'll run a targeted canary with Acme on Wed/Thu and reconvene on Friday for go/no-go.

I'll update the release notes and product checklist after Laura confirms the customer comms.

Thanks —
Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Product Manager, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference
